summary.name: Jenni
summary.one_liner: Jenni is an AI academic writing and research assistant that helps students and researchers draft papers, search sources, and add citations inside a purpose-built editor.
use_cases: Drafting essays and academic papers with cited sentences
Building a literature review from imported PDFs
Searching for relevant papers across 200M+ indexed works
Checking claims in a manuscript against its sources before submission
Formatting in-text citations in APA, Chicago, IEEE, or other styles
Co-authoring and sharing drafts with supervisors
summary.what_it_does: Jenni lets users import sources by dragging in PDFs or importing from Zotero or Mendeley, or by searching a claimed 200M+ paper index. Its AI autocomplete suggests sentences that it says are grounded in the user's sources and can be traced to the exact page and paragraph in the PDF. Inline citations are added in one click across 10,000+ citation styles, and documents can be exported to .docx, LaTeX, or HTML. A Reviews feature analyzes claims against sources and flags issues such as unsupported or overstated claims, plus proofreading suggestions. The page also lists recent additions including code execution in chat, figure and table cross-references, viewer and commenter sharing roles, and AI-generated charts.
notable: Claim-level links from AI-suggested sentences to the exact location in the source PDF
Autocomplete can be restricted to the user's own curated library rather than general web data
Reviews feature flags unsupported, overstated, and contradicted claims before peer review
Live collaboration with inline comments, version history, and commenter/viewer roles
caveats: Pricing and plan details are not stated on the page
Page text contains marketing claims such as '10,00+' and '10m+' figures that are not independently verified
Listed in eudk/awesome-ai-tools as aimed primarily at students
